record: Sponsored the AWARE Act (H.R. 5360), directing the Federal Trade Commission to publish guidance on AI chatbot companions for parents, educators and minors.

Authored the SAFEBOTs Act (chatbot disclosure to minors, crisis hotline information, break prompts); it and the AWARE Act were included in the KIDS Act (H.R. 7757), which passed the Energy and Commerce Committee.

Listed among House members supporting the discussion draft of the Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 (Obernolte and Trahan), a federal AI framework setting a national standard over state laws.
grade_reason: She has spoken repeatedly about AI, but only about chatbot risks to children and about competing with China under one federal standard; nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk. Her 2026 statements (KIDS Act, March 2026; Great American AI Act draft, June 2026) are level D.
notes: All six required web searches ran this time, plus two more (Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act cosponsors; her AI remarks in 2026). None of the topic searches returned anything linking her to superintelligence, extinction, a pause or slowdown, China talks or AI safety in the catastrophic sense. Sources on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, Casar) name only Democratic cosponsors; none shows her as a sponsor or cosponsor, though the full congress.gov cosponsor list was not opened. No House letter about AI risk signed by her was found (the many-signer letters are handled centrally and were not searched). Earlier run: the official press release listing at houchin.house.gov was read from November 2026 back to April 2025, and AI-related releases were opened and quotes checked; those quotes are kept. A November 2025 Kids Online Safety Caucus quote (D) was dropped to keep at most three D statements, in favour of the June 2026 one. The June 2026 quote is from a Ripon Advance news report dated 8 June 2026 (page text downloaded and checked); the statement may have been made a day or two earlier with the draft's release. Her 2026 KIDS Act release quote speaks of 'new technology powered by Big Tech' without naming AI, so it was left out. Her Breitbart op-ed (22 November 2025) and a Punchbowl News event remark (May 2026, seen only as a paraphrase in a search summary) concern children's safety, innovation and aligning with the Senate; not quoted.
